rv.q: Idle Muse creates a performance which is funny, unsettling, and deeply human.

Old Scratch, otherwise known as the devil – the small “d” is important here – has chosen the village of Edmonton as his latest venue in which to harvest souls. Only there’s nothing “old” about Scratch ( Nathaniel Kohlmeier ) here; this Scratch is a young, handsome, thoroughly charming and witty man.
I highly recommend Idle Muse's WITCH.

Beyreis and her ensemble understand how to balance the contemporary locutions in Silverman’s dialogue (peppered with phrases like “What’s the BFD” and “on the DL”) with the material limitations and communal prejudices of the 17th-century world in which it’s set, which makes Witch about as timely as you can get.
Caty Gordon's performance is excellent from the outset, but it grows until it becomes perhaps the best one of the lot, yet another of the play's canny surprises.
This is a generous show packed with many pleasures, challenging ideas, great storytelling, wit and humor, and solid acting and production.
